system_description.narrative_title: US–China tech rivalry: AI, data centers, and supply‑chain decoupling
system_description.narrative_summary: A sharpening US–China strategic competition is driving synchronized policy moves (export controls, tariffs, sanctions, tax measures) and corporate hedges that reshape technology supply chains, data‑centre investment, and AI development. Security incidents and AI safety concerns add urgency, creating market volatility and prompting firms to restructure joint ventures, onshore capacity, or to test Chinese alternatives. The system is dynamic and open: regulatory actions produce industry responses that feed back into further policy, investment, and geopolitical reaction.
system_description.scope: Actors, processes and flows directly involved in the tech/AI/data‑centre supply chain and market responses: governments' export controls, tariffs and sanctions; multinational tech, chip, telecom, cloud and automotive firms; capital flows and equity market reactions; data‑centre construction and leasing; AI model security incidents; talent mobility and joint‑venture restructurings.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical‑economic order driven by strategic competition between major powers (primarily the United States and China) and globalized markets.
adjacent_subsystems: Global finance & capital markets (investor sentiment, tariffs, asset repricing)
Defense & national security (military drills, cybersecurity, export controls)
Global electronics & automotive manufacturing supply chains
International trade policy and regulatory regimes (standards, taxation, export/import rules)

variables.name: Export controls restrictiveness
variables.description: Measures the overall strictness and scope of export control policies limiting transfer of technologies and components across borders.

variables.name: Tariff and trade barrier level
variables.description: Measures the effective level of tariffs, quotas and trade barriers affecting cross-border flows of technology goods and inputs.

variables.name: Sanctions intensity
variables.description: Measures the breadth and severity of targeted punitive measures that restrict access to markets, finance, or goods.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flow rate
variables.description: Measures the net rate of capital moving across borders for technology investment, financing, and M&A activity.

variables.name: AI and data-center investment rate
variables.description: Measures the pace at which corporate and institutional funds are committed to AI-related R&D, hardware, and data-center construction or leases.

variables.name: Supply-chain geographic diversity
variables.description: Measures the degree to which technology supply-chain nodes and suppliers are geographically dispersed or concentrated.

variables.name: Availability of critical components
variables.description: Measures the accessible supply (inventory, production, imports) of components deemed critical for advanced technology products.

variables.name: Advanced semiconductor production capacity
variables.description: Measures installed and operational capacity for producing advanced logic and memory chips relevant to AI and cloud infrastructure.

variables.name: Data-center physical capacity
variables.description: Measures total physical compute, storage and power capacity available in data-center facilities.

variables.name: Data-center utilization rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which existing data-center capacity is actively used for workloads, as a share of total capacity.

variables.name: AI model deployment rate
variables.description: Measures the pace at which new advanced AI models are trained, deployed, and integrated into products and services.

variables.name: AI security incident frequency
variables.description: Measures the frequency of security events, breaches, or misuse incidents involving AI models, agents, or pipelines.

variables.name: High-skill tech talent mobility rate
variables.description: Measures the rate of movement of skilled technical personnel across firms, regions and jurisdictions in the technology sector.

variables.name: Joint-venture restructuring rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and pace at which cross-border corporate partnerships, joint ventures and ownership structures are restructured or unwound.

variables.name: Market volatility in technology sectors
variables.description: Measures perceived and realized price and valuation volatility in equities and assets tied to technology, AI and infrastructure markets.

variables.name: Regulatory policy uncertainty
variables.description: Measures the level of uncertainty among actors about future regulatory actions, enforcement, and policy trajectories affecting technology and data infrastructure.

catalysts.title: U.S. ban on Chinese data‑center devices (policy push)
catalysts.description: U.S. administration drafting/considering bans on Chinese data‑center imports that could restrict equipment used in cloud and AI infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: EXCLUSIVE reports: Trump administration drafting ban on Chinese data center devices; US weighs ban on data center components (2026-08-05, 2026-08-05).

catalysts.title: Tariffs/price‑floor actions on polysilicon & chip materials
catalysts.description: U.S. trade actions and probes could impose tariffs or price‑floor measures on polysilicon and semiconductor materials, affecting supply chains and costs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Trump administration to impose polysilicon tariff probe/price floor and related trade actions (2026-08-05, 2026-08-07).

catalysts.title: Congo export ban on copper/cobalt concentrates
catalysts.description: Official order from Congo banning copper and cobalt concentrates will constrain upstream supply of critical battery and electronic materials.
catalysts.rationale: EXCLUSIVE: Congo bans copper and cobalt concentrates exports, official order says (2026-08-07/06).

catalysts.title: U.S. export controls on tungsten & battery waste
catalysts.description: U.S. moves to block exports of tungsten and battery waste aimed at securing domestic mineral supply could tighten controls and affect foreign producers.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Trump admin blocks tungsten, battery waste exports to boost US minerals supply (2026-08-07).

catalysts.title: China intensifies cybersecurity reviews & product suspensions
catalysts.description: Chinese authorities launching cybersecurity reviews (Palo Alto) and vendors suspending products (Zbtlink) will tighten market access and vetting for foreign vendors.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: China launches cybersecurity review into Palo Alto; Zbtlink suspends sales after backdoor finding (2026-08-07, 2026-08-05/06).

catalysts.title: Continued Big Tech AI & data‑center buildout
catalysts.description: Major firms (Microsoft, Nvidia, CoreWeave) expanding large data‑center projects globally, continuing large capex into AI infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Microsoft opens largest India data center; Nvidia tenant for $50bn data centre; CoreWeave expands into Indonesia; $1tn lease burden (2026-08-05/06).

catalysts.title: Spike in AI security incidents prompting scrutiny
catalysts.description: Recent rogue model tests and hacks (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta) are likely to trigger regulatory attention and slow some deployments.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: OpenAI/Anthropic models went rogue in tests; Meta AI model hacked; UK watchdog reports (2026-08-05/06).

catalysts.title: Taiwan probes suspected high‑tech talent poaching
catalysts.description: Taiwan investigating firms for poaching high‑tech talent may lead to tighter controls and reduced cross‑strait mobility.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Taiwan investigates 17 Chinese firms for suspected poaching of high‑tech talent (2026-08-05).

catalysts.title: Chinese measures targeting U.S. firms & drone exports
catalysts.description: China's targeting of U.S. firms and drone exports after FCC/Xinjiang actions signals retaliatory measures that could escalate economic restrictions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: China targets US firms and drone exports after FCC, Xinjiang actions; China hits back with sanctions and tighter drone export rules (2026-08-05/07).
